Trigger when the heart rate falls below the threshold

1. A watch that measures your heart rate, paired with Gadgetbridge on this phone, with continuous heart-rate measurement turned on.
2. In Gadgetbridge, turn on the automatic database export and choose where it goes.
3. In Gadgetbridge, Settings → Intent API: allow the activity sync trigger and the database export.
4. Below, choose that same export file.
Gadgetbridge is not installed. Install it from F-Droid first.

It takes about a minute: Gadgetbridge syncs the watch and exports first.
Choose Gadgetbridge\'s export file in the Pulse tab.

The watch stopped sending your heart rate; the switch fired on %s.
Watch alert: the switch fires at %s unless you press \'I\'m OK\'.
These actions run on your PC when the switch fires. Test them once with a safe folder before trusting them.
Could not send the magic packet: %s
SSH password (if there is no key)
Destroy a key file or folder

Keep the sensitive folder encrypted (VeraCrypt, LUKS, EFS, 7-Zip AES…) with a key that lives at the path below. When the switch fires, the key is overwritten twice and deleted, leaving the data locked for good.
Key file or folder path on the PC
Full Windows path, e.g. C:\\Users\\me\\Desktop\\test. Drive roots, whole user folders and system folders are refused.

Two passes over every file, written in place (zeros, then random data), and then the file is deleted. Anything that cannot be overwritten is left where it is and reported. Folders are removed once empty. On an SSD the firmware may keep old copies, so destroying the key above is safer.
After the other actions, send \"shutdown /s /f /t 0\" over SSH.
SSH host, user, or key or password missing.
Key path refused as unsafe; nothing touched.
Folder path refused as unsafe; nothing touched.
The path does not exist on the PC.
The path is a link; it was not followed.
The path is a file, not a folder.
%1$s; anything that could not be overwritten was left in place.\n%2$s
The email will really go to %1$s, and these PC actions will run: %2$s. It is exactly as if the deadline had passed.
Full path, e.g. /home/me/test. The root, whole home folders and system folders (/etc, /usr, /var…) are refused.
After the other actions, run \"sudo -n systemctl poweroff\" over SSH. The SSH user needs sudo without a password for that command, or polkit permission to power off.
shred is not installed on the PC (it comes with coreutils).
Right after Wake on LAN, this runs on the PC over SSH, in PowerShell, as the SSH user. It can have several lines. No window opens: what it prints shows up in the result notification.
Right after Wake on LAN, this runs on the PC over SSH, in bash, as the SSH user. It can have several lines. No window opens: what it prints shows up in the result notification.

plurals.name: pulse_rule
plurals.item: If the last reading is below the threshold, an alarm goes off and the switch fires %2$d minutes later unless you press \'I\'m OK\'. A normal reading after the alarm calls it off.
If the last %1$d readings are below the threshold, an alarm goes off and the switch fires %2$d minutes later unless you press \'I\'m OK\'. A normal reading after the alarm calls it off.

resources.string: This provider only accepts an app password: 16 letters that you create for this app. Your usual password is refused.
This does not look like an app password (16 letters).
Proton only sends over SMTP with an SMTP token, which exists for addresses on your own domain with a paid plan. Put the username and token that Proton gives you in User and Password.
Outlook, Hotmail and Microsoft 365 no longer accept a password for sending, and this app cannot sign in to Microsoft yet. Use another provider.
The server asks for an app password, not your usual one. Create one with the button below the password and paste it there.
The server did not accept the user or the password. The user must be your full email address and, with Gmail, Yahoo or iCloud, the password an app password.
Microsoft refused the password: it no longer allows sending with one. Use another provider.
Sign in with a key (safer, and no password needed) or with the password of that user on the PC.
On the PC, add the public key to C:\\ProgramData\\ssh\\administrators_authorized_keys if the user is an administrator, or else to .ssh\\authorized_keys in the user\'s folder.
On the PC, add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of that user.
